The strongest ground is that the promise was oral. Many states require a signed writing to revive a debt the statute of limitations has barred, so the oral promise is unenforceable there. Lack of consideration is weaker, since Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 makes a promise to pay a barred debt binding without new consideration, and the overheard "deadbeat" remark neither supplies consideration nor creates duress.

CONFIDENCE: 62
